LocalCheck — PR #77 current-state review

Review baseline: October 17, 2026 · head d018a570624bd3b96ee606f585dfaa5e5cc6d5aa · read-only.

PR #77 contains useful engineering improvements, but it does not deliver the final design agreed in this conversation. The largest problem is that the implementation and its checked-off tracker are following an older agreement. Several explicit later choices are missing or contradicted. The attached HTML has the correct latest commit label, but only six screen views; it is not a complete PR record or proof that the app is finished.

1. What is actually under review

  • PR #77 is open and unmerged, targeting main. Its eight commits include the earlier #75 court-flow changes. Comparing current head with main gives 88 changed files, 7,513 additions and 5,062 deletions. Many lines are a form being moved, shared components, tests and documentation—not 88 screens.
  • Latest commit: d018a57. It changes 21 files. Its player-facing changes are mainly contrast, bottom-tab label colors, Settings/LocalPlus fine print and heatmap number contrast; much of it adds local visual QA and completion rules.
  • CI at this exact head succeeded. Its jobs include typecheck/unit tests, web bundle compilation and a docs-update check. The Expo PR preview workflow also succeeded. This establishes a buildable branch, not native visual acceptance or production release.
  • This review inspected the complete file diff, current critical source files, the attached HTML images at full size, the earlier screenshot workbook/handoff, and the attached launch-plan text and embedded mock pages. No mobile app source, database, score, challenge, check-in, production release or PR status was changed.
  • Deployment boundary: source is verified at the SHA above. The HTML says its captures came from that preview, and its visible UI is consistent with the source. I did not independently verify a fresh native install or that any old browser preview URL now serves that exact commit. An Expo preview existing is not the same as a production update being delivered or accepted on a device.

Version: yes. Completeness: no. Its heading names d018a57, which is the reviewed head. It contains 12 images: raw and marked-up versions of six views, all described as 393×852.

Missing from the record: onboarding; View Court Live/Games/Players/Week/Info; Explore list and working map; collapsed and expanded drawer; scheduled game 3v3/full 5v5/started/result; Log Game and team/entered-score states; Me Activity/Friends/Inbox; dedicated challenge states; another player’s head-to-head/activity/actions; notifications; QR and review-rules sheets. The record explicitly says there are no before captures. It therefore cannot prove which changes improved or regressed between commits, or quantify the latest contrast improvement by eye. 4. The final decisions that must carry forward

These are the latest explicit choices from this chat and the final DEVELOPER-HANDOFF.md, not a new redesign proposal:

  • Home = Feed + Upcoming. Feed has the active-player row above activity. Upcoming uses the selected daily timeline combining planned visits and games. The timeline mock is titled Schedule, but its destination is Home Upcoming.
  • Standalone Schedule = the large week heatmap. Seven days across; 6 AM–midnight down; favorite court dropdown; accessible Add Time/plus and Schedule Game. Match selected mock composition with the expressly corrected axes, no Busiest sentence, stronger attendance count and better use of height.
  • Home actions at the top: check-in/out plus small Court; no Plan or bottom action stack. Conroe replaces the house. No house remains beside the city.
  • Favorites: one free favorite/local court, multiple paid favorites, switching on Home and Schedule. No paid maximum was specified.
  • Locals on the court page, Elo ordered. Do not add unselected rank/newest filters. Home no longer needs Locals.
  • Understated feed markers everywhere: quiet compact tiles, small arrival/departure dots, VS/calendar distinctions. No glowing orange login/logout tiles. Normalize checkout/played information order. Normal-size h with spacing; soften interfering header art.
  • Court-specific page is a data view: remove check-in and Plan Visit there. Check-in belongs on Home and Explore drawer; availability creation belongs on standalone Schedule.
  • Preserve Explore’s card/drawer continuity. Fix clipped names and peek. Its daily chart has no heading/day label/arrows/Busiest copy. Home arrows were later allowed; that does not cancel the drawer-specific instruction. Do not remove Recent Activity just because it was circled.
  • Challenge states share a dedicated lifecycle destination. Generic Log Game is for impromptu logging. Improve inbox spacing. Keep full result actions reachable.
  • Log Game: Final Score immediately above submit; extra roster rows above; no WIN/LOSS ELO commentary; remove duplicate inline YOU; retain overall Compete structure.
  • Head-to-head verdict stays. Appearance was criticized; deleting it was expressly rejected. Compare variants before making another style decision.
  • Onboarding: stable centered/blended art and lower cleaner fields; U.S. map/location or address; orange top-down court rectangle; confirm; existing Add Court dolly/tilt/rotate; truthful auto-check-in choice; enter app without separate alerts step. Do not delete notification capability from the product.

The full ledger gives 40 stable issue IDs, current implementation, evidence and a concrete acceptance check. Open style choices are marked as choices; they are not silently converted into approvals.

5. What fell off, and what actually regressed?

Clear missing final scope: Home Upcoming; favorites/entitlements and Home court switching; selected Schedule composition; city replacing house; moving Home actions up/removing Plan; quiet feed markers; removing Court actions; quiet drawer chart; dedicated challenge destination; pinned score block; removing ELO commentary; simpler onboarding flow/copy and requested map camera transition. These are not minor polish leftovers.

Changes visible in the PR that run against the latest lock: moving hero actions into the bottom stack; replacing a text local marker with the house choice; introducing the smaller h; introducing brightly outlined/glowing arrival tiles; deliberately changing recent-vs-older event hierarchy. Some were based on earlier alternatives. The error is carrying them forward after the later decision superseded them. Where I cannot establish a previously shipped approved version, I call this a decision mismatch rather than claiming a production regression.

Inherited problems not fully repaired: accepted-ranked challenge redirects, Court check-in/planning duplication, ELO outcome sentence, duplicated YOU, long Settings helper. The PR changes surrounding UI but does not fix these requested items.

Known remaining defect: the author’s latest comment reports intermittent small-phone drawer clipping. A tracker row says the drawer settles correctly while another row says it still intermittently does not. A change cannot be accepted as fixed on that evidence.

Unverified reported defect: username editing/focus problem. The input is disabled while saving, but source review does not reproduce the reported inability to edit; it remains a reproduction task, not a confirmed fix or invented root cause.

No evidence of loss in this PR: subscription prices, starter/referral/Pioneer awards, score privacy server rules, production data isolation and native geofence implementation are not rewritten here. They still need release checks, but this UI diff does not prove those features regressed.

6. Why the process kept producing this result

The decision record and the latest agreement diverged. D57 explicitly chooses house/no-favorites and bottom Plan/Check-in/Court. Those contradict the final owner instructions. A later agent can follow the repository “correctly” and still build the wrong product. D57 must be superseded explicitly, preserving history, not silently rewritten as if the earlier choice never happened.

Documentation checks establish that a file changed, not that it is true. CI’s docs job passes, while CURRENT_STATE says Schedule never scrolls and a later paragraph says it scrolls on short phones. The tracker marks old-target items done. There needs to be one acceptance ledger tied to the final decision and exact commit.

The new visual check is valuable but narrower than its headline. It renders 38 states at three sizes against mocked data. It does not judge approved layout, tone, redundant copy, art placement or real native behavior. It has no dedicated challenge lifecycle screen or expanded drawer state, and onboarding stops at welcome/name. It aborts external network, so it cannot validate real map rendering. Optional tab clicks can do nothing without asserting the intended target state.

Passing a ratchet does not mean the interface meets the target. The committed baseline permits 445/523/543 sub-11px text detections, 305/343/378 sub-44px target detections, and 1/2/2 low-contrast detections across the 38 states at each size. These are repeated browser detections, not unique defects; native hitSlop and larger text need separate assessment. A passing run means counts did not increase, not that all existing debt was fixed. The known drawer failure also means a clean all-pass visual run is not established.

The evidence set is incomplete. Six current screenshots, no before images, no native keyboard/gesture/safe-area proof. Useful evidence, but insufficient for the new definition of done or for saying every screen is accepted.

My judgment: good component consolidation and some real correctness fixes; incomplete product alignment and insufficient acceptance evidence. Keep the useful work. Do not call this final visual polish against the latest brief, and do not restart a broad redesign to fix the mismatch.

7. What the October 8 launch plan establishes

The supplied file has 43 PDF pages. Its snapshot still describes build 33/version 1.0.3 and PRs around #65/#66; it is historical input, not the current release state. I extracted its text and inspected the embedded mock pages 23–26 (score, onboarding/avatar, profile/LocalLegend, friend/challenge).

Preserve its durable rules: only Jesse merges; builds/releases need explicit control; checked boxes require implementation and verification; truthful counts and private/test data; real drawer behavior; editable visible username; friends-only challenges; casual challenges are scheduling without score; side-specific score hiding; one local court free; opt-in geofence with hold/Undo; website and store copy reflect the product.

Do not revive superseded details: onboarding sport helper copy, city-only search, old header/card styling or separate alerts step just because an older PDF contains them. The latest specific instructions override those. The PDF itself also revises casual games from scored games into plans, demonstrating why explicit supersession is necessary.

The large court import, intentional seed launch, partnerships, App Store copy/assets, reviewer readiness and App Clip exploration remain separate workstreams. PR #77 supplies none of those deliverables. Their status is “not established by this PR,” not automatically “never done anywhere.”

8. Managed next steps

Batch 1 — reconcile scope before further polish. Use LC-01–LC-08, LC-11–LC-14 as the accepted Home/Schedule/favorites contract. Supersede D57 and related PRODUCT/DESIGN passages. Implement only the already selected target; favorites require a scoped persistence/entitlement change, not a simulated dropdown. Preserve court header progress and good shared controls.

Batch 2 — repair flow and copy failures. LC-22–LC-26 and LC-30–LC-35: challenge destination, score placement, redundant strings, onboarding sequence and map treatment. Keep the verdict and Compete structure. Prove each meaningful state, including denied permissions and entered scores.

Batch 3 — acceptance and release evidence. Close drawer clipping; capture current SHA before/after at 375/393/430, working maps, expanded drawer, full teams, error/empty/loading, larger text and native keyboard/safe areas. Use approved reference beside actual screen. A status becomes accepted only when evidence for its ID is attached. Source done, browser verified, native verified, merged and released are separate statuses.

Carry-forward rule: this report is the review snapshot; DECISION-LEDGER.csv is its trackable ledger; FILE-BY-FILE.md is its immutable-head inventory. In the next turn, first compare PR head to this baseline. If it changed, review only the delta and update affected IDs and evidence. Do not regenerate the whole story or mark rows done from prose alone. No new design choice is required to start the already locked fixes.

Evidence limits

I did not run the mobile app’s pnpm suite locally; the supplied workspace is the website project, while PR #77 belongs to LocalCheck_Expo. I verified successful GitHub CI for the exact head instead. I did not perform a fresh signed-in native or browser walkthrough in this review; visual conclusions refer to the attached current record, historical owner evidence and inspected source. Actual phone behavior, current production/OTA installation, payments, data permission enforcement and transition motion remain unverified here.
